title: Thermodynamic Limits of Quantum Search
summary: Modern cryptography relies on keyed symmetric ciphers to ensure the secrecy and authenticity of high bandwidth data transfer. While the advent of quantum computers poses a challenge for public key cryptography, unbroken ciphers are considered safe against quantum attacks if their key is sufficiently long. However, concrete bounds on the required key length thus far remain elusive: Despite the well known asymptotic complexity of Grover's quantum search, the optimal algorithm to recover a secret key, no implementation-agnostic tight bounds were established.
